reasoning:
I'm reading the pocket sizes they reported, 4.90 to 5.30 mm, and those look like effective across-flats after the ribs are counted. Against a 5.5 mm nut, even the largest of them leaves about 0.2 mm of interference, and the 5.1 mm one leaves 0.4 mm, which seems like too much.

I'm weighing whether to ask the user which coupon pocket actually held the nut, since the reported numbers alone don't settle how the ribs were counted. Building steps from slight clearance to slight interference and marking them clearly seems like the safer route, and asking them to measure would tell me more than the feedback so far has.

reasoning:
Without feedback to lean on, I want the design to hold up on its own. The 4.9, 5.1, and 5.3 values look like they measure the pocket as across-flats minus twice the rib height, though the ribs at 30, 150, and 270 degrees aren't opposite each other, so I'm not sure. A 0.4 mm interference at nominal might be too tight to press in by hand. PLA holes usually print about 0.1 to 0.15 mm undersized, so I'm weighing a plain hex at 5.5 mm plus 0.1 mm.

I'm going to lower the knob's rib height to 0.2 so the ribs only crush from print shrinkage, and widen the coupon range to 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3. I also want a lead-in chamfer so the nut can start by hand, plus a note in the manual on what to watch for. The ribs will run from the floor up to the nut top, so the nut gets about 0.4 mm of free travel before it reaches them.

    af=p.nut_af+p.pocket_clear

        b=b.cut(cq.Workplane('XY').workplane(offset=H-depth).polygon(6,af/math.cos(math.pi/6)).extrude(depth+1))
        b=b.cut(cq.Workplane('XY').circle(p.bolt_clear_d/2).extrude(H+1))

    return out
